title: Union Avoidance Fails over Finite Fields — But Cyclic Vectors Still Exist
description: Over F_2, the three 1-dimensional subspaces cover all of F_2^2, showing union avoidance fails for |K| <= n. Despite this, the cyclic vector theorem holds for ALL fields via the structure theorem for f.g. modules over PIDs. Includes explicit F_2 counterexample and annihilator-based characterization.

overview.historicalContext: The union avoidance lemma (finitely many proper subspaces don't cover V over infinite K) has been the standard tool for proving cyclic vector existence since Hoffman-Kunze (1961). But over small finite fields, this fails: F_q^n can be covered by proper subspaces when q <= n.
overview.problemStatement: Show that union avoidance fails over F_2 (explicit counterexample), and prove that the cyclic vector theorem still holds for all fields via module theory.
overview.proofStrategy: Section I: Enumerate F_2^2 and show 3 proper subspaces cover it. Section II: Define the annihilator polynomial and prove it characterizes cyclic vectors. Section III: State the field-independent theorem via the structure theorem.

conclusion.summary: Explicit F_2 counterexample showing union avoidance fails, plus the field-independent cyclic vector theorem statement. The counterexample is fully proved; the main theorem requires the PID structure theorem.
openQuestions: Prove the PID structure theorem in Lean 4
